title: Packaged sidecar launch crashes for extensionless service names
reasoning: In packaged mode, resolvePythonScriptPath only adds candidates when the requested script ends in .py or .pyc. If resolveSidecarLaunchTarget is called with an extensionless service name and no packaged binary exists, scriptPath becomes undefined, then path.dirname(scriptPath) throws while building the launch target. The same extensionless input works in dev mode because the dev branch always joins the normalized name under src/main/python, so this is a packaged-only contract mismatch.
reproduction: Call resolveSidecarLaunchTarget('sidecar_service') in packaged mode when no sidecar binary exists; resolvePythonScriptPath returns undefined and path.dirname(undefined) throws.
recommendation: Normalize extensionless script names before packaged script resolution, for example by treating them as .py inputs and resolving the corresponding .pyc, or explicitly reject extensionless names with a clear error before calling path.dirname.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the excerpt shows no test coverage for packaged-mode path resolution or extensionless service names.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a main-process unit test that stubs packaged mode/resourcesPath, calls resolveSidecarLaunchTarget with both 'service.py' and 'service', and asserts both resolve to the same packaged .pyc fallback or both fail with a deliberate typed error.
minimumFixScope: frontend/src/main/runtime_paths.cjs plus focused tests for packaged resolveSidecarLaunchTarget input normalization.
